newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says joblessness to fall slowly - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says joblessness to fall slowly - paper.

text.p: Argentina's unemployment rate will fall by no more than one point by next May, according to Economy Minister Roque Fernandez quoted by the Clarin newspaper Tuesday.

"Only by the survey in May next year will a strong fall in unemployment be apparent. And when I say strong I mean a fall in the rate of one point, no more," Fernandez told Clarin in London, where he is leading a trade mission.

"Currently a rise in the level of employment has been registered, as shown by the statistics done by the Labor Ministry. But it is still insufficient to make up for the amount of people who want to join the labor market," he said.
Argentina's unemployment rate was 17.1 percent in May, when the last published survey was carried out. The results of the latest survey, carried out in October, are due out soon.
President Carlos Menem said recently that the unemployment rate would fall below 10 percent in the survey this October.
Fernandez said he had met envoys of top banks in London to complain of what he described as an unfairly high risk rating assigned to Argentina, which puts it below Mexico and Brazil.

"This does not seem fair to me, taking into account the magnitude of the structural reforms we have carried out over the past few years," he said. "This rating is the result of a confused evaluation of some factors and it damages us because it makes us pay a higher rate to place our public debt."
